note: RFC 9687 Section 4.3 stops SendHoldTimer following any transition out of Established as part of resource release. Re-read all four tagged functions: SendHoldExpiryRunsTheEvent29ActionList now joins exact ErrSendHoldTimerExpired and requires timer disarmed after expiry; TeardownStopsTheSendHoldTimer starts armed, sends local Cease and requires disarmed; PeerDrivenTeardownStopsTheSendHoldTimer starts armed and drives received NOTIFICATION and peer TCP close, joins Run, then requires not Established and disarmed; NoSendHoldExpiryLeavesTheSessionIntact advances one nanosecond short of expiry and requires armed, Established and no close. The completion-only Run receive in the peer-driven cases is appropriate because the release predicates are state and timer, not a common error identity across two different terminal causes. Session.closeConn stops SendHoldTimer at the shared close boundary, and Run retires session timers on every exit. Thus the unenumerated hold/error exits share the judged stop boundary rather than independent untested stop implementations. No state or timer assertion was removed by the join comments or exact-sentinel edit. Source audit only; no native observation claimed.
